books.section: Topic 6.10 Development of the Middle Class

primary_sources: Montgomery Ward and Company stereoscopic card, Chicago

stimulus.text: The image is a hand-colored stereoscopic card, one of a “Travelers Series” published by Montgomery Ward and Company of Chicago. It shows the firm's large Chicago building twice, side by side: a tall tower rising over a many-windowed block with an arched ground floor. Printed beneath the two views is the caption “Class A, No. 12. The Establishment of Montgomery Ward and Co., One of the Sights of the City, Chicago, Ill., U. S. A.”
stimulus.source_note: Stereoscopic view of the Montgomery Ward and Company establishment, Chicago, from the Robert N. Dennis collection of stereoscopic views. Public domain image from Wikimedia Commons; viewed by the writer.

stem: What does the caption printed beneath the two views call the Montgomery Ward building?

options.text: The tallest building in the world
options.misconception: The caption says nothing about height records.

options.text: A factory for making steel rails
options.misconception: The caption calls it an establishment and a sight, not a factory.

options.text: The home of the Chicago city government
options.misconception: The caption names Montgomery Ward and Company, not the city government.

options.text: One of the sights of the city

rationales.A: Tallest in the world appears nowhere in the caption. Read the printed words.
rationales.B: The caption says “The Establishment of Montgomery Ward and Co.” It does not call it a factory.
rationales.C: The caption names the firm, not the city government.
rationales.D: The caption reads: “The Establishment of Montgomery Ward and Co., One of the Sights of the City, Chicago, Ill., U. S. A.”
rationales.general:
Quote the caption, not your guess about it.
1. Find the printed caption beneath the two views.
2. It names the firm: Montgomery Ward and Co.
3. It then calls the building one of the sights of the city.
4. That phrase is the answer, word for word.
Remember: when a question asks what a caption says, the caption itself is the evidence.
